reasoning: The word is MSA in origin, but in everyday Ramallah speech ق is usually a glottal stop. Shadda on ت gives ittifaa'. Some speakers keep q in formal or political registers.
fii means 'there is'. In spoken urban Palestinian, ث in the MSA-origin word حادث is usually s, so 7aadis. Careful or news speech may use th.
ط is emphatic T. Ramallah speakers say wasT il-balad, or just il-balad, for the town centre.
The Palestinian past he-form is mishi, not MSA mashaa. The English 'walked' fixes the verb reading, not the adjective 'maashi'.
A Levantine proverb that Palestinians use freely. 3een has long ee, iid has long ii, and ق is a glottal stop. Taa marbuta after ر and ص is a, giving baSiira and 'aSiira.
ص is emphatic S. The word is religious and in everyday use, and the ة is written as a long aa in the word.
Spoken Levantine for the Netherlands is hulanda, with a short vowel after l. The written alif after ل may stand for a different vowel in this dictionary's source, hence low confidence.
Geminate verb, he-form past: 7ass, as in 7ass bi-. The final s is doubled.
Standard Palestinian greeting. khayr becomes kheer with long ee. The article loses its vowel after the vowel-final masa.
إذا is said iza, since ذ becomes z in this word. bti7taaj is the masculine b- present. ishi means 'something', and rannili is the imperative of ranna (form II, to phone) plus li.
Long oo in yoom. The literal sense is 'the day of Thursday'; speakers often say just il-khamiis.
ض is emphatic D and ع is 3. A common colloquial phrase in Palestinian speech.
Form I past, he divided, with ق as a glottal stop. Everyday speech often prefers the form II 'assam, but the unmarked spelling and the English fit form I.
Form X past, he-form. The initial hamza is a vowel seat, so it is not written in the romanization. ح is 7.
An MSA-origin noun that Palestinians use in conversation, with short u and a sukun on z. It is somewhat elevated in register.
In a possessive compound the taa marbuta is pronounced t, so shanTa becomes shanTit. ط is emphatic T.
A cultural term from MSA that Palestinians use in conversation, as in it-turaath ish-sha3bi. Final ث is kept as th in this register; some speakers say s.
English loanword adapted to Arabic syllable structure. Initial hamza is a vowel seat. Some speakers say internet with e in the first syllable.
'Warned' is form II, 7azzar, with doubled z. ذ becomes z in Palestinian speech, as in 7azzartak 'I warned you'.
Negative command built on ma plus the form III verb waakhad, 'hold it against'. ذ becomes d in this native verb. The masculine form has no final -i on the verb.
ع is the clipped form of على, joined to il-'aakhir. The glottal stop of آخر is kept. It means 'all the way, to the fullest', as in ta3baan 3al-'aakhir.
oDa (from Turkish) is common in Palestinian speech. In the possessive compound the taa marbuta is pronounced t. The article assimilates to ن, giving in-noom with long oo.
la- plus 7aal plus the suffix -o, 'his'. It can also mean 'on his own'. The Ramallah suffix is -o.
mumkin is used in Palestinian conversation. n'ajjil is the 'we' present of form II 'ajjal. The medial hamza is a glottal stop and the shadda doubles j.
Hollow verb, he-form past, with long aa and ع as 3.
